extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, science editors, authors, reviewers, and research-integrity professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Announcing and describing the ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 Peer Review Terminology standard intended to provide shared definitions and simplified language for peer review roles and practices in journal article publishing to improve transparency and comparability. Aimed at encouraging adoption by journals and publishers to support open research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified terminology for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 standard 'offers a simplified terminology that will make the peer review process more transparent to authors, reviewers, and readers across the journals that adopt it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to standardize language so stakeholders understand what peer review model or role is being used; this simplification is meant to facilitate clearer communication across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for open research
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard is intended to 'support open research by simplifying the communication of peer review roles and practices.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting the terminology standard is presented as a measure that will enable openness around how peer review is conducted, aligning with broader open-research initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster greater transparency and fairness in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: With the move toward open research and new peer review models, concerns about fairness have increased; the standard aims to 'foster greater transparency in the peer review process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, shared terminology is positioned as a remedy for opaque or inconsistent descriptions of peer review that can contribute to perceived unfairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared definitions of peer review roles and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'shared set of definitions will also enable the community to compare peer review processes across publications more easily.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized definitions should be used by journals and publishers so that roles (e.g., reviewer types, editorial roles) and practices (e.g., blinded, open review) are comparable and unambiguous across venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: developed for articles and journal publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The new standard 'was developed for articles and journal publications,' with the note that a NISO Standing Committee may address books and other peer‑reviewed research content in future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should treat the standard as targeted primarily to article/journal workflows at present and watch for future extensions before applying it to other publication types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based development and working-group input
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard builds on STM's initial set of definitions and best practices and incorporated 'practical information' from many pre-publication trials and the input of STM and NISO working group members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard reflects both consensus workgroup deliberations and empirical trial outcomes; implementers can cite this provenance when justifying adoption and should consider similar trialing in their contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free availability and encouragement of implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Peer Review Terminology Standard is freely available from NISO (link provided) and NISO expresses readiness to 'support implementations of this new standard.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the standard is freely accessible, journals and publishers are encouraged to consult the document directly and pursue implementation with support from NISO and community working groups.
